cards.back: A statement of no effect or no difference, assumed true until the data give evidence against it (H0).
The claim that there is an effect; what we accept if we reject the null hypothesis (H1 or Ha).
Probability of getting results at least as extreme as observed, assuming the null hypothesis is true.
Rejecting a true null hypothesis (false positive); probability = alpha.
Failing to reject a false null hypothesis (false negative); probability = beta.
1 − beta: probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when the alternative is true.
The threshold for rejecting the null hypothesis, commonly 0.05.
One-tailed tests for an effect in one direction only; two-tailed tests for an effect in either direction.
The p-value is below alpha, so we reject the null hypothesis. It does not mean the effect is practically important.
Larger sample size, larger effect size, higher alpha, lower variability.
Compares the means of two independent groups; assumes roughly normal data and similar variances.
Compares the means of two related measurements on the same subjects (before/after).
Tests whether two categorical variables are associated, using a contingency table.
Analysis of variance: tests whether three or more group means differ, using the F statistic.
Measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship; ranges from −1 to 1.
A correlation between two variables does not show that one causes the other; a confounding variable may explain it.
The line that minimises the sum of squared residuals: ŷ = b0 + b1x.
Observed y minus predicted y (y − ŷ) for a data point in regression.
The predicted change in y for a one-unit increase in x.
The predicted value of y when x = 0; may have no real meaning.
The proportion of the variance in y explained by the regression model.
When predictors in a multiple regression are highly correlated with each other, making the coefficients unstable.
Residuals plotted against fitted values; a random scatter suggests the linear regression model fits.
Using a regression line to predict outside the range of observed x values; unreliable.
An outlier has a large residual; an influential point changes the regression slope a lot when removed.
A nonparametric correlation based on ranks; measures monotonic relationships.
Regression for a binary outcome; models the log odds as a linear function of the predictors.
Symmetric, bell-shaped distribution described by its mean μ and standard deviation σ.
In a normal distribution about 68% of values fall within 1 standard deviation of the mean, 95% within 2 and 99.7% within 3.
(x − mean) / standard deviation: how many standard deviations a value is from the mean.
The normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
The number of successes in n independent trials, each with the same probability p.
Fixed number of trials n, two outcomes, independent trials, constant probability of success.

cards.front: Mean and variance of a binomial distribution
cards.back: Mean = np, variance = np(1 − p).
Counts of events in a fixed interval when events occur independently at a constant rate λ.
A long tail to the right; the mean is greater than the median.
Every value in an interval is equally likely.
Like the normal distribution but with heavier tails; used when σ is unknown; depends on degrees of freedom.

cards.front: Expected value of a random variable
cards.back: The long-run average: the sum of each value times its probability.
A range of plausible values for a population parameter: estimate ± margin of error.
If we repeated the sampling many times, about 95% of the intervals would contain the true parameter.
Critical value × standard error; half the width of a confidence interval.

cards.front: What makes a confidence interval narrower?
cards.back: A larger sample size, a lower confidence level, less variability.
σ/√n: the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean.
For large samples the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal, whatever the shape of the population.
The distribution of a statistic (like the sample mean) over all possible samples of the same size.
Every group of n individuals in the population has the same chance of being chosen.
Divide the population into strata and take a random sample from each stratum.
Divide the population into clusters, randomly choose whole clusters, and sample everyone in them.
When the sampling method systematically favours some outcomes, e.g. convenience sampling or voluntary response.
Bias when people chosen for the sample do not respond and differ from those who do.
A parameter describes a population; a statistic describes a sample.
Resampling the observed sample with replacement to estimate the sampling distribution of a statistic.
The middle value of ordered data; resistant to outliers.
Q3 − Q1: the spread of the middle 50% of the data.
The typical distance of values from the mean; the square root of the variance.
The average squared deviation from the mean.
Shows the five-number summary (min, Q1, median, Q3, max) with outliers marked.
A value below Q1 − 1.5×IQR or above Q3 + 1.5×IQR is flagged as an outlier.

cards.front: Mean or median for skewed data?
cards.back: The median, because the mean is pulled toward the tail.
A bar chart of a quantitative variable, showing counts in bins.
